topics.topic: Authoritative number of data_provider tables
questions: Does `data_provider` have exactly three model-backed tables, or all six tables enumerated here?
Does “three tables” limit the dependency to three tables, or are all six listed tables authoritative?
Does data_provider own three typed tables or the six tables enumerated here?

quotes: `models`, for exactly the row models and enumerations of its three tables:

`ArtifactTypeOwner` (a type with its owner service) and `ServiceName` for
`ARTIFACT_TYPE_OWNERS`; `ServiceRight` (a service and an operation) with
`ServiceName` and `ServiceOperation` for `SERVICE_RIGHTS`;
`ServiceHighestClass` (a service and its highest class) with `ServiceName`
and `DisclosureClass` for `SERVICE_HIGHEST_CLASSES`; `PersonalDataField` (an
answer model's name and a field's) for `PERSONAL_DATA_FIELDS`;
`RefusalHttpStatus` (a code and its status) with `RefusalCode` for

path, whether it is a change and whether it touches an uploaded file) with
`OwnerAction` for `OWNER_ACTIONS`. Its other constants are scalars and
import nothing.
judgement.divergence: One implementation limits the dependency to three model-backed tables; another imports and constructs all six enumerated tables, which the generated module and strict-import validation observe.

questions: What is the complete authoritative set of rows, including sign-in, sign-out, reads, confirmation steps, import mapping/upload/confirmation, and every other owner action?
What are the complete rows of OWNER_ACTIONS: every OwnerAction value, its exact HTTP method and path, and its change and uploaded-file flags?
What are the complete OWNER_ACTIONS rows: every OwnerAction member, HTTP method, path, change flag and uploaded-file flag?

topics.topic: Exact wire constants, scalar types, and name comparison rules
questions: What exact string and type does each of `OWNER_TARGET_PARAMETER`, `OWNER_CSRF_FIELD`, and `OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` hold, and are those names stable wire contracts across releases?
What exact string value and scalar type does each constant have, and what encoding and comparison rules apply to those names?
What exact wire strings do these three exported constants contain?

quotes:
The target is the query parameter
  `OWNER_TARGET_PARAMETER` (`target`) names, an identity and never a
  personal value (R0-29).

The CSRF value is the field
  `OWNER_CSRF_FIELD` (`csrf`) names, the upload's first part included, and
  `OwnerRequest.csrf_value` carries it from the form's reading to the
  request's admission, since a body is read once. The session cookie is
  named `OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` (`__Host-registry_session`): set
  `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `Path=/` and no `Domain`, which the `__Host-` prefix
  makes a browser require (A13 rule 1), and `SameSite=Strict`, so a browser
  never sends it with a request another site started (owner, 2026-11-24;
  OWASP).
judgement.why: State 6 fixes the three wire strings and specifies how the target, form field and cookie are carried.

topics.topic: Request facts retained or erased after unreadable input
questions: Does "no values" remove only decoded body/form fields, or also the route action, query target, session cookie, CSRF value, and other successfully read headers?
Does “no values” discard only body/form values, or also a previously parsed target, cookie, method/path action and headers, and which operation is invoked if the action itself cannot be determined?
What does “no values” erase, and which request facts remain available to operations: action, method/path, query target, session cookie, CSRF value, headers, revision and declared file metadata?

quotes:
The session identity from the cookie; the CSRF value; the request — which
action or page, its target, its stated revision or access version, its
values, a confirmation value; for sign-in the credential; for an upload the
file part's declared length, which `upload_framing.read_upload_head`
derived, or none, and the file part as an unread stream that ends where the
part ends, which `owner_interface` hands on without reading and this
operation passes, unread, to `migration_import.read_import_mapping`, which
alone consumes it within the request.

A request whose body, upload head or
form cannot be read is handed on with no values, no CSRF value and no
credential, nothing partly read kept: it is admitted or refused by the
ordinary checks, a change refused at stage (1) for its missing CSRF value,
a sign-in as a missing credential (owner, 2026-11-24; option (a) of the
question State 4 round-51 and round-55 T3 carried to State 7).
judgement.why: The later surface contract separates the session identity and routing request from values, and expressly clears values, the CSRF value and the sign-in credential on a read failure.

topics.topic: Connection-owner handling and signaling after an unreadable request
questions: After sending the answer, who owns the decision to drain the unread body, keep the connection reusable, or close it, given that `instance_lifecycle` owns the HTTP connection and `owner_interface` may not know it?
Which module owns the decision to produce a response rather than close the connection after a body/head read failure, and what signal must owner_interface return to that connection-owning module?

quotes:
`instance_lifecycle`'s two listeners share one HTTP implementation. Each
connection's socket waits at most the imported
`LISTENER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (30) for the next bytes of a request — its
headers or its body, an upload's head and file among them; a wait that
reaches it ends the stream with a failure, which the reader sees as any
stream failure: an upload's head then gives no CSRF value (refused at stage
(1)), its file part `file_unreadable`, and the connection is closed. A
request answered before its body was read to its framed end — any request,
not an upload alone — has the remainder discarded unread and its
connection closed; a connection carries a next request only after one whose
body was read to its end.
judgement.why: State 6 assigns connection handling to `instance_lifecycle` and requires unread remainder to be discarded without reading and the connection closed after the answer.

topics.topic: Exact read_upload_head signature and result model
questions: What is the exported function's exact signature and result model, including how it returns the CSRF value, declared file length and lazy file stream, and how it distinguishes another form, an overlong head, malformed input, EOF and I/O failure?
What is the exact result type of read_upload_head, including how it distinguishes a valid upload, another/oversized form, an I/O or syntax failure, and a later file-stream failure?

quotes:
`upload_framing.read_upload_head` reads the head alone,
  at most `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES` (8192 bytes) — the boundary from the
  content type, the CSRF part, the file part's headers — and answers
  `UploadHead`: the CSRF value, the delimiter `\r\n--<boundary>` that ends
  the file part, and the file part's declared length — the request's
  declared length less the head read and the closing delimiter with its
  final `--\r\n` — or none of them.

A
  stream that ends before the delimiter makes its `read` raise, a failure of
  the stream that `read_import_mapping` answers `file_unreadable`, as any
  stream that fails; a request that declares less than the head and the
  delimiter answers an `UploadHead` with none of its values.
judgement.why: State 6 defines the `UploadHead` result, collapsed head-failure representation and the distinct later failure of `MultipartFileBody.read`.

topics.topic: OWNER_ACTIONS method/path matching, uniqueness, and failure behavior
questions: How are method and path matched, what uniqueness constraints apply to rows, and what action or refusal results when no row or more than one row matches?

How are the request method and path compared with OWNER_ACTIONS, including case, percent-encoding, trailing slashes, repeated slashes and query strings, and what happens when no row or more than one row matches?

judgement.why: Method/path normalization, comparison, uniqueness and unmatched-route behavior are wire-format and contract rules assigned to State 6 rather than module ownership in State 3.

topics.topic: Response behavior when listener timeout causes a request read failure
questions: Does this obligation include a body or upload-head read that fails because `LISTENER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` expires, despite the listener rule saying it closes the connection when the next bytes do not arrive?
Does a timeout while reading an owner request close the connection without an answer, or is it an unreadable head/body that must receive an operations answer?

quotes:
The timeout is a wait for progress, not a deadline for the request: it
applies to each read of the socket and restarts with every byte that
arrives, so a slow client that keeps sending is never cut, and one that
stops for `LISTENER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` is. It is the socket's own timeout,
measured by the operating system; `clock` does not time it, and a suspension
of the host counts as whatever the operating system counts it as (A13 rule
2's monotonic readings are the sessions', not the listeners'). A wait that
reaches it while the headers are read closes the connection with no answer
and reaches no surface. One that reaches it while a body is read is a
failure of the body's stream: what its reader has already handed on stands
— a session check already made, with its restarted 30 minutes, an admitted
change already committed — and the reader answers the failure as it answers
any stream failure (an upload's head no CSRF value, its file part
`file_unreadable`); the answer is sent if the connection still takes it,
and the connection is then closed.
judgement.why: State 6 distinguishes a timeout during headers, which closes without an answer, from one during a body or upload stream, which is answered if possible and then closed.

topics.topic: Handling failure of an upload file stream after a valid head
questions: When a valid upload head has been handed to migration_import but the file stream ends before its delimiter, must migration_import return file_unreadable or must owner_interface discard the request values and redispatch it as an ordinary valueless operation?

quotes:
A stream that ends before the closing delimiter is a failure
of the file part's stream, which `migration_import` refuses as a file that
cannot be read (`file_unreadable`), replacing nothing kept (A16 rule 2).
judgement.why: The text expressly assigns failure after a valid head has been handed on to the file-part stream and requires `migration_import` to return `file_unreadable`.

topics.topic: Target value representation and unambiguous decoding by action
questions: What is the target value's representation for each action, especially actions whose subject contains more than one identity, and how is it decoded without ambiguity?

quotes:
The target is the query parameter
  `OWNER_TARGET_PARAMETER` (`target`) names, an identity and never a
  personal value (R0-29). A `GET` request's other fields are its query's, a
  `POST` request's the fields of its `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`
  body, or of the upload's multipart head. Each field is named by its path:
  an `OwnerRequest` or `OwnerValues` field by its name, a nested model's
  field by its parent's path, a full stop and its name, a tuple's element by
  its parent's path, a full stop and its position from 0, and a union's
  variant by its discriminator among its fields; a field's text is the
  field's value for text, an enumeration member's value, `true` or `false`,

topics.topic: Whether a failed upload counts as session activity
questions: When an upload head fails or exceeds its bound, has the owner request "arrived" for A13's session-validity and idle-time refresh rules?

quotes:
An upload arrives, for the session
check, once its head has been read (A13 rule 2).

a stream that fails or ends before its
declared length is refused as `file_unreadable`, replacing nothing kept and
changing nothing of the session but the instant of its last request, which
every request carrying it moves (A13 rule 2) — and an
unreadable or malformed one is refused with its kind alone.
judgement.why: The later texts make head completion the upload's arrival point and state that even an unreadable request carrying the session moves its last-request instant.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
